title: An August 2008 draft existed — title and abstract survive; the FILE does not
claim: A draft titled "Electronic Cash Without a Trusted Third Party" was linked, not attached, to Adam Back on 20 Aug 2008 and Wei Dai on 22 Aug 2008. Its title, full abstract and Hashcash citation at [5] are preserved verbatim inside Back's witness statement. Back downloaded it, later searched for it, and swore he could not find it.

evidence.what: First Witness Statement of Dr Adam Back, 17 July 2023 — §5 quotes Satoshi's email in full (title, abstract, Hashcash at [5]); §6 'I believe I did download the paper at the time'; §7 b-money 'was not mentioned in the pre-release draft he sent me'; §11 'I don't think I have a copy … I haven't been able to find one from the checks I have made'
evidence.where: COPA v Wright [2024] EWHC 1198 (Ch), Exhibit AB1 / witness statement C/9

evidence.what: Wei Dai to Bird & Bird, Oct 2023: the three published emails are the entirety of his communications with Satoshi
abstract text as preserved (hash of the text, not of the file)

notes: NOT LOCATED, and now closed against both named recipients by their own sworn or published words. What is lost is the FILE - the bytes, and whatever the body said between abstract and references. What survives is adjudicated: the title, the complete abstract, the Hashcash citation at [5], and sworn confirmation from its only known reader that b-money was absent. No hash of the file exists anywhere, so a recovered candidate could never be verified cryptographically - only by those four discriminators plus custody. A reconstruction built from the correspondence is already in circulation and would pass the wording tests by construction; the reference numbering is the discriminator that matters.

title: The file id Satoshi linked is bracketed to within days by an unrelated crawl
claim: Satoshi emailed a LINK, not an attachment, to Adam Back on 20 Aug 2008 and Wei Dai on 22 Aug 2008: upload.ae/file/6157/ecash-pdf.html. That host's file ids are sequential, and the Internet Archive crawled it through 2008 for unrelated reasons. Ids 6145, 6160 and 6161 - immediately either side of 6157 - were all first captured on 23 August 2008, placing 6157's upload on or before that date.

evidence.what: 2,421 upload.ae file ids across 14,810 captures (2008-2010) via the Wayback CDX API; independently corroborated by a third party's own extraction of 17,255 upload.ae URLs listing the same nearest neighbours, 6145 and 6160
Satoshi's emails quoting the URL (Exhibit AB1; Wei Dai correspondence)

reproduce: curl -s 'http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=upload.ae&matchType=domain&output=json&from=2008&to=2010&fl=timestamp,original&limit=40000'   # use a HIGH limit; at 8000 the neighbours truncate away
notes: Corroborates TIMING only. It does not recover the file, say anything about its contents, or identify who uploaded it. Its value is that the bracketing party had no interest in the question: the Internet Archive crawled an Emirati file host in 2008 for its own reasons. Note also that it captured 6145, 6160 and 6161 that day and never captured 6157 - consistent with an unlisted upload whose URL travelled only by private email, though a crawl gap has many innocent causes. The file itself was never archived and structurally could not be: the download sat behind a form POST, which crawlers do not submit.

title: The 11 November 2008 whitepaper is created — WE DO NOT HOLD IT, BUT WE CAN NOW RECOGNISE IT

notes: STILL THE PRINCIPAL OPEN ITEM as an artifact -- but no longer an open-ended search. VERIFIED 7 Aug 2026: both hashes were re-read from the original Appendix PM3 PDF and are present verbatim -- the SHA256 is a contiguous 64-character string. (A page header falls between the 'SHA256:' label and its value in the extracted layout, which is what prompted the earlier caution; the value itself is unbroken.) title: A court judgment states the 2009 transaction count
claim: The COPA v Wright judgment records that there were just 219 non-coinbase transactions in the 32,489 blocks created up to the end of 2009 — the same figure our independent query returns.

evidence.what: judgment paragraph 716, held in our own archive
our query returning 219

notes: Independent confirmation from an adjudicated source. Recorded also because we held this document while believing the count was unpublished — the figure was in our own archive and we did not connect it.

title: Two unmodified 2009 binaries mine and relay a block on the historical genesis
claim: Two copies of the released January 2009 bitcoin.exe (fbcac071…), in network-isolated VMs discovering each other over the client's own hard-coded IRC path, re-derive genesis 000000000019d668…; one mines block 1 at real difficulty 1 and the other validates and accepts it, ending with byte-identical block files.

evidence.what: the two-node witness, with the raw block-file digests
both nodes' blk0001.dat after the run

notes: Graded PARTY-RELEASED, not CHAIN: this is our own record of our own run. What a reader can check independently is the binary's hash and that the genesis it re-derives is the real one. It establishes behaviour of the 2009 client, and nothing about who wrote it.

title: The 2009 client performs a real chain reorganisation
claim: Partitioned, the two nodes mine competing chains; on reconnect the shorter node's unmodified binary fires *** REORGANIZE ***, orphans its own valid block and adopts the longer chain, both converging on tip 000000004e442b… at height 15.

evidence.what: the reorganisation run

notes: The losing node retains its orphan rather than discarding it - an exact +223-byte on-disk delta, one v0.1 block. Difficulty never left 1, so nothing here measures hashrate or difficulty dynamics.

title: A second Bitcoin genesis is mined, on a chain of its own
claim: Genesis 00000000ad12f3ecd9b14e4276ac98936fb0d658f05dce95ad35d18fceee208a is mined at difficulty 1 by the released January 2009 client, its coinbase quoting The Times of 3 August 2026 - a separate chain, network magic f00ba726, not interoperable with the 2009 one.

evidence.what: the chain, its parameters and its release
re-derive either genesis in the browser, same code path for both

reproduce: python derivatives/bitcoin/net.py   # re-derives the genesis from its parameters
notes: Not the 2009 chain and not a fork of it: its own genesis, its own network, no inherited balances, and its units are not historical satoshis. NOT money - no premine, no sale, no value assigned. The coinbase headline is a newspaper front page of that day, which fixes the earliest date the block can have been made; the OpenTimestamps row fixes the latest.

title: A matured coinbase is spent and relayed — and maturity is 120 blocks, not 100
claim: Transaction f4309c… spends a coinbase that matured under the client's own rule - main.h sets COINBASE_MATURITY = 100 but main.cpp:544 withholds a generated coin for twenty blocks beyond it - created on one node, accepted by the other across the wire, and mined into block 00000000b4ca03f9… at height 122.

evidence.what: the relayed spend, both nodes' logs and the block it landed in

notes: The 100-vs-120 discrepancy is a property of the 2009 source, not of this run: the constant and the code that uses it disagree, and the code wins. Value transfer on the unmodified 2009 client is executed here rather than modelled - on a chain where the value is zero.

title: A published Bitcoin client is shown to have mined its own chain's blocks
claim: Blocks 2, 3 and 4 of the 2026 chain were produced by bitcoin-0.1.3 (c3f15fc5…), the client published under that tag; block 4 sits inside a 39-minute window bracketed by before-and-after captures sharing one PID and one process start time.

evidence.what: the release, its signature and its timestamp proofs
block 4 and its binding record

notes: What the binding establishes is that a process running a binary of a known hash was alive before and after the block's timestamp - NOT that this process mined this block. No artifact can tie a nonce to a PID. A narrow bracket is a stronger statement than a wide one; it is not a proof. The same claim this project makes about Satoshi's fbcac071…, made about ours, at the same strength and with the same limit stated.

title: The chain outruns its evidence set — NOT YET SEALED
claim: The sealed evidence set for the 2026 chain stops at block 4. Block 5 was mined at this timestamp and the chain has continued past it; every block beyond 4 has no published findings, no hash manifest and no binding record. This row deliberately names no current height — the height moves, the gap is what persists.

evidence.what: the live anchor's reported tip

notes: Marked NOT HELD against ourselves, on the same rule applied to everyone else on this page: the event demonstrably happened and we do not hold the artifact in publishable form. Graded NONE because a status file we generate is not independent support for our own chain. The reproduce command reads the live height rather than this row asserting one, so the row cannot go stale while the miner runs. It will be upgraded when the blocks are captured and sealed, and not before.

title: The 2026 chain's release is anchored in the 2009 chain
claim: The Bitcoin-v0.1.4 release artifacts are committed to Bitcoin block 961652 (00000000000000000000b286970ddbb501ced552e95c7ceda6ab92cf0f44fdbc) through OpenTimestamps, proving they existed no later than that block.

evidence.what: block 961652 - merkle root the proofs resolve to
.ots proofs published with the release

reproduce: ots verify bitcoin-0.1.4.tar.gz.ots   # or walk the proof and match block 961652's merkle root
notes: The only 2026 row graded CHAIN, and it earns it on the 2009 chain rather than on ours - the proof is backed by mainnet proof-of-work, not by us. It fixes the LATEST date these artifacts can have; the newspaper in the 2026 coinbase fixes the earliest. This project declines to treat the satoshin@gmx.com key's self-asserted 2008 date as evidence, so it anchors its own artifacts rather than asking for a weaker ruler than it hands everyone else.
